# Close checklist and dependency levels

Trim to the business. A five-day close is a common target for mid-sized teams; small businesses can often close in one or two sessions.

## Before month end (last 2 to 3 business days)

- Share the close calendar and deadlines with contributors.
- Confirm cut-off with payables, receivables, payroll and treasury.
- Do a preliminary bank reconciliation for all but the last days.
- Review open purchase orders for accruals; collect notes on unusual transactions.

## Dependency levels

| Level | Tasks | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Record cash receipts and payments; bank statement; payroll entries and accrual; depreciation; prepaid amortization; payables accrual; intercompany postings | Nothing; starts on day 1 |
| 2 | Bank reconciliation; revenue recognition; receivables and payables subledger reconciliations; foreign exchange revaluation; remaining accruals | Level 1 entries |
| 3 | All balance sheet reconciliations; intercompany reconciliation; adjusting entries from reconciliations; preliminary trial balance | Level 2 |
| 4 | Tax provision; equity roll-forward; consolidation and eliminations; draft statements; preliminary variance analysis | Level 3 |
| 5 | Management review; final adjustments; period lock (by a person); reporting package; forecast update | Level 4 |

Critical path: cash, payables and receivables entries, then subledger reconciliations, then balance sheet reconciliations, then tax provision, then draft statements, then management review, then period lock.

## Typical five-day calendar

| Business day after month end | Main work |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Level 1 entries |
| 2 | Revenue, remaining accruals, subledger reconciliations, revaluation |
| 3 | Balance sheet reconciliations, intercompany, preliminary trial balance and variances |
| 4 | Tax provision, draft statements, detailed variance analysis, management review |
| 5 | Final adjustments, period lock, reporting package, retrospective |

## Status values

Not started, In progress, Complete (reviewed), Blocked (name the blocker), At risk (may miss its date).

## Close metrics worth tracking

Close duration in business days; adjusting entries after the soft close; late tasks; reconciliation exceptions; corrections found after close.

## Retrospective questions

What went well? What took longer and why? What blocked us? What surprised us in the results that we should have caught earlier? What can we automate next month?
